title: Tactical inference conversion scripts - draft
body:
Purpose and audience:
- Quick-reference sales scripts for AE/SE during discovery and technical qualification.
- Target: midmarket to enterprise PLG/Platform buyers (platform teams & infra engineering).
- Not a polished deck — intentionally short, skimmable, and script-first. Field-friendly.

One-page framing (internal TL;DR):
- Opening (20–40s): "Most teams we talk to can’t consistently predict inference cost or latency under real traffic. Redwood gives a single API and runtime that makes those tradeoffs visible and controllable across hosted/dedicated/private deployments."
- Value hooks: predictable unit economics, simple fallback/routing for reliability, and fast dev experience for model rollouts.

Suggested 3-slide mini-deck (for quick demo calls):
1) Problem + How customers are solving it today
   - Fragmented: model owners run ad-hoc endpoints; infra teams script autoscaling templates; product teams overprovision GPUs to avoid tail latency.
   - Pain bullets: unpredictable token spend, noisy latencies, complex rollouts, audit/compliance gaps.
2) Redwood’s tactical lever set (what we actually operate on)
   - Routing policies (latency/cost/region), automatic prefix/KV caching, quantization profile suggestions, and canary rollouts with automatic fallback.
   - Quick example: a docs-search workflow where caching reduces median token cost by ~40% while preserving 95th pct latency.
3) Call to action + next steps
   - Quick POC: 2-week test with sample traffic, one integration route in the app, baseline + post-optimization metrics.

Conversation starters and quick conversions (scripts):
- Discovery openers: "How do you measure unit-cost per inference today?" / "Tell me about a recent outage/latency incident and how the team handled fallback."
- If they push hard on accuracy: "We keep model output stable during batching/caching changes and surface regression alerts tied to your prompt set — can you share a small sample of typical prompts?"
- If security/compliance is raised: "We offer dedicated and private deployment options with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs — which compliance standards are you targeting? SOC2? HIPAA?"

Top technical objections and short responses (field-friendly):
- "We already host models in our infra" → "Totally common. Teams that adopt Redwood see a reduction in ops overhead from custom batching/kv-cache code and gain predictable SLOs across dev/staging/prod. We can run in private mode so control stays with you."
- "Quantization will break quality" → "We recommend per-workload quantization profiles and run lightweight evals on your prompt set before rollout; rollback and canary are built in."
- "We can’t expose tokens/cost metrics" → "Redwood supports role-based access and token-level telemetry can be scoped to project/team — sharing aggregated econ metrics is sufficient for most engagements."

Competitive talking points (short):
- Vs. generic cloud endpoints: explicit inference economics controls + built-in workload-aware batching reduces per-token spend by design.
- Vs. model-hosting vendors: unified API across hosted/dedicated/private so product code doesn’t need rework for deployment mode.
- Vs. self-built: removes the need to maintain kernel/compilation optimizations and reduces SRE time spent on throughput tuning.

Quick demo checklist for SEs (5–10 mins):
- Show API call time vs. token breakdown in console (token, model, routing cost).
- Toggle a routing policy and show simulated fallback to cheaper variant.
- Show a canary rollout page and regression alert sample.
- Point to Optimize suggestions (batch sizes and quantization) and show projected cost delta.

POC template (2-week, high-level):
- Week 0: kickoff + capture sample traffic (1–3 endpoints) + grant access to small dataset of prompts.
- Week 1: integrate SDK or API route, baseline metrics collection, baseline evals on prompt set.
- Week 2: apply 1–2 optimizations (caching, batching, quantization profile), run canary, measure delta, present results + recommended commit size.

Pricing & negotiation cues (field notes):
- Hosted: lean on per-token economics and demoed cost deltas from Optimize.
- Dedicated: emphasize commit sizing and guaranteed throughput; use customer’s 95th percentile throughput to size a proposal.
- Private: role in deals where compliance or networking isolation is mandatory — position as platform + services bundle.
- Discounts: aim to trade headcount/commit length for runway; offer a 3-mo pilot credit in exchange for usage telemetry access.

Open questions / TODOs for deck iteration:
- Need one new slide with concrete benchmark for a LLM-augmented search use case (we have internal numbers but must anonymize). TODO: get sanitized metric set from Applied ML (JIRA-INF-1189).
- Add a short script for SMB-focused reps that do not have a technical SE on the call.
- Validate claim language around "40% unit cost reduction" with PM/research.

References & field links:
- Internal prep: CONFLUENCE-1234 (playbook skeleton)
- Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/58
- Related battlecards: quick-ref for objections in sales repo (will link final ID)

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep examples real but short — field hates fluff.
- Use customer anecdotes in final deck (ask CS for 2 anonymized wins).
- Try a one-page PDF variant for AE Slack + a 3-slide deck for SE screen share.

Revision history (working):
- 2025-01-10: initial sketch (this file).
- 2025-01-22: added POC template + pricing cues (Liam).
- 2025-02-02: cleaned objection responses and added TODOs (Asha).

Contact for reviews: Maya Patel (owner), reach out in #g2m-sales or DM for rapid changes.
